### Observed differences

- Activity A01 was not observed in any of the 200 earlier-window traces. In the later window it appears in about 31 of 200 traces (roughly 16% participation), with about 0.3 occurrences per trace on average — so it typically occurs once in the traces where it appears at all [OCC001].
- In the later window, when A01 occurs it sits around two-thirds of the way through the trace by event position (median about 0.70, middle half of positions roughly 0.51–0.88); no position data exists for the earlier window because A01 was never observed there [POS001].
- In the later window, the observed outgoing flow from A01 splits between two successors: about 54% of its observed outgoing transitions go to A09 and about 46% to A10 (57 transitions observed). No outgoing transitions were observed earlier, again because A01 itself was not observed [DIR001].

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that A01 became an executed part of the process in the later window: an activity that was absent from the earlier sample now runs in roughly 16% of cases, once per affected trace, around two-thirds through the trace by event position, and continues to either A09 or A10 in roughly equal shares. This rests on three agreeing items that all concern A01 — participation rising from zero to about 31 in 200 traces [OCC001], position support appearing only in the later window [POS001], and outgoing transitions to A09 and A10 observed only in the later window [DIR001] — while the screening produced 3 qualifying control-flow items against only about 0.17 expected if nothing had changed, more than an unchanged process would typically yield.

Limitations: zero participation in the earlier window only shows A01 was not observed there; the evidence cannot rule out that A01 already existed at a very low frequency (too rare to appear in 200 traces) and merely became more frequent, rather than being genuinely new. Positions are event steps, not clock time, so no claim about timing is made. The three items describe the same activity and are not independent confirmations.

Other differences: none beyond the appearance of A01 are present in the evidence.

Screening: 34 units tested, 3 items qualified, 0.17 expected by chance. 3 items is many times larger than 0.17 (about 18x). So the count is not what an unchanged process typically produces. So we move past the "insufficient evidence" screening gate.

All three items concern activity A01:
- OCC001: A01 participation went from 0 to 0.155 (about 31 in 200 traces in the later window), mean occurrences per trace 0 → 0.285. Before support 0, after support 31.
- POS001: A01 position — before support 0 (never observed), after support 0.155, mean position ~0.66 of the trace. So A01 appears in the later window at around two-thirds through the trace.
- DIR001: outgoing transitions of A01 — before profile empty (A01 never observed), after: A09 ~54%, A10 ~46% (57 outgoing transitions observed across 31 traces... actually support after 57 outgoing transitions).

So the behaviour: A01 was not observed at all in the earlier window (0 of 200 traces), and in the later window it appears in about 31 of 200 traces (about 16%), typically once (mean 0.285 occurrences per trace), positioned around two-thirds through the trace, and from A01 the flow continues to A09 (about 54% of observed outgoing transitions) or A10 (about 46%).

Hypothesis: A01 was added to the process (became part of the process / newly executed) in the later window — an activity added / became present. This is a participation change: an activity that was absent is now present in a minority of traces. This is directly supported by OCC (participation 0 → 0.155), POS (appears at position ~0.66), DIR (its outgoing edges observed).

Is this "Supported hypothesis" or "Weak hypothesis"? The evidence directly shows A01 absent before, present after. The screening count: 3 items vs 0.17 expected — many times larger. All three items describe the same underlying difference (A01 appearing). The hypothesis "A01 was added / became executed in the later window" is directly supported: participation evidence shows zero → nonzero. Zero participation only means the activity was not observed in that window — so a competing explanation is that A01 existed but was rare enough to not appear in 200 before-traces. That's a competing explanation the evidence cannot fully rule out: A01 might have existed before at a very low frequency (below detection in 200 traces). Hmm. With 200 traces before and 0 occurrences, if the true participation were, say, 1%, we'd expect ~2 occurrences; observing 0 makes very low frequency plausible but not zero. So the competing explanation: A01 was already present but very rare before, and its frequency increased. Either way, there's a change in participation (from not observed to observed in ~16% of traces). Actually the hypothesis "A01 became executed / was added" vs "A01 was rare and became more frequent" — both are changes in participation. The evidence supports a change in participation of A01 directly.

Given the guidance: "Changes in participation ... can support a hypothesis that part of the process is executed more often, less often, skipped or repeated differently". Zero participation only means the activity was not observed in that window. So the hypothesis: A01 is executed in the later window in about 16% of cases, whereas it was not observed before — i.e., A01 was added or its execution frequency increased from (near) zero. This is directly and consistently supported by three agreeing items (OCC, POS, DIR) all about A01, and the screening count (3 vs 0.17 expected) is many times the chance expectation.

I'd say "Supported hypothesis": the evidence directly shows A01 absent → present. The limitation: we cannot distinguish a genuinely new activity from one that was previously too rare to appear in 200 traces; also its position (POS uses event positions, not clock time) — we can say it appears around two-thirds through traces in terms of event position, not that it was "moved" there.
